text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Friday.

GERMANY - Bund futures off earlier highs as profit-takers take toll, Buba, German Finmin deny EMU delay remours. U.S. Q4 GDP revision due at 1330 GMT, Chicago PMI at 1500 GMT. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 103.33, down 0.31 from Thursday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended sharply lower on a combination of factors, including the Wirral South by-election, the softer tone on other markets, interest rate pessimism and pre-weekend profit-taking. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 112-14/32, down 25/32 from Thursday's settlement price.

FRANCE - March bond future ends off highs as U.S. bonds fail to hold gains after data. Traders said market seen capped at beginning of next week ahead of U.S., German jobs reports. The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 132.42 up 0.02 from Thursday's settlement price.

ITALY - The March Liffe Btp future extended early losses, falling over 100 basis points down through support at 129.50 and 129.15 due to technical reasons linked to the contract's expiry and roll-over into June on March 4. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 127.80 down 1.99 from Thursday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - US Treasuries shift back to minus column in choppy trade. Fed Gov Meyer emphasis on "pre-emptive (rate) policy" in news report cited as negative. Earlier, slippage in Chicago PMI prices paid, employment indices lifted market out of negative territory.The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-26/32, up 2/32 from Thursday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.81 percent.

JAPAN - Japanese government bond futures ended up but off their intraday highs as position-adjustment sales emerged. Weak stock market and short-covering pressure ahead of benchmark shift provided support.In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 126.36, down 0.02 from Thursday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market saw a string of sterling deals hit the screen on Friday morning which included the launch of the second sterling global bond. FHLB set the ball rolling with a 300 million stg June 2002 global bond. Vodafone followed suit with a 250 million stg seven-year issue and LB Schleswig-Holstein with a 100 million stg three-year bond. Meanwhile Russia's long-awaited mark Eurobond is expected to be launched within the next two weeks.
